catalog_record.scan_author: Minneapolis Institute of Art; model building and customization by Lou Brown
catalog_record.scan_source: Museum photogrammetry and surface-reflectance research; Mia, UW-Stout and Cultural Heritage Imaging
catalog_record.note: This seated yogini embodies female divine power. A jar and wand suggest healing, while her poised body conveys control of breath and movement. The sculpture once occupied a circular open-air temple with other yoginis.

catalog_record.title: Shiva with Garland, Seated under a Maithuna Couple
catalog_record.source_institution: Grinnell College Museum of Art / Grinnell College Immersive Experiences Lab
catalog_record.scan_author: Amy Kan; Grinnell College Immersive Experiences Lab (GCIEL)
catalog_record.scan_source: Creaform Academia 50 scan, 6 August 2024; processed in VXelements and VXModel 10
catalog_record.note: A seated Shiva carrying a garland occupies the lower part of this sandstone relief. An intimate couple appears above him. The Grinnell College Museum of Art identifies the sculpture as an Indian work of the eleventh or twelfth century.
catalog_record.attribution: Shiva with Garland, Seated under a Maithuna Couple. Artwork: Unknown Indian artist; 11th–12th century.
